Stir up the struggle which is beneficial to the
class demands of students (such as improving curriculum,
making better preparation, selecting teachers and
securing freedom of speech). (Great 60).

Instead of causing the students to focus
their attention on a dismissed girl student (girls
are behaving thus) you should direct them to turn their
viewpoint to the welfare of the whole body of students
(such as the students demands mentioned in the Ka-moh's
letter - freedom for self study, publicity of finances,
dismissal of bad teachers, betterment of curriculum,
and freedom of speech and assembly). (Great 60).

Persist in various thought struggles among students,
break the reactionary work of the various cliques of the
Kuomintang and the 3rd Party, as well as repudiate
their logical mistakes. (Great 124).

There are some day-students in the Tung Yang
School who are under our direction. You should
also lead them to join in the daily struggle. Such
slogans as demanding freedom of selecting teachers,
assembly, organization, speech and publication, are
all capable of stirring up their daily struggles.
The Party books and publications should be offered
for sale among students with a view to consolidating their
revolutionary will. (Great 4).

You must strongly determine to reorganize branches
among factories in order to carry out their works
and make them center power of the masses. Correct
their mistakes of neglecting small struggles.
Do not miss the opportunity of a quarrel over a copper
or a dispute over slight ill-treatment of workers by
foremen. A small quarrel or suspension of work by
a foreman over division of money, is struggle.
Struggle is not necessarily in the form of a large strike.
If there is a possibility, a strike will naturally
be declared. (Great 153).

- 50 -

Relation between Struggle

Constant attention should be paid to the daily
life and economic interests of the labour and peasant
masses. Peasants struggles should always be organized
using any cause however trivial as an excuse.
From these minor clashes they will be led to political
struggles through economic struggles such as refusing
to pay rentals. While the small struggles are being
extended and united into a major struggle, the masses
besides benefiting by the enrichment of their struggle
experience, will become more animated in spirit and
their faith in us will be more firmly established
thereby stabilizing the foundation and strengthening
the struggle force of our Group. (Great 72).
At the same time we should also pay our attention
to relation between the struggles of labourers, and
the struggles of soldiers and the struggles of peasants.
Every comrade should exert his efforts in these
activities and participate in every struggle be it
small or large, in order to receive training,
increase his experience as well as to establish a
formidable understanding of 'class' in his mind.
(Great 72).

Extend the small struggles which are organized from
demands in the interests of labourers and peasants as
a basis and arouse the spirit of the masses of the two
aforementioned classes with a view to transforming the
economic struggles into anti-Kuomintang and anti-Imperialist
struggles. In time of carrying out struggles special
notice should be paid to the organization of the Party
and the masses, and through these struggles, the
labourers and peasants are to be induced to realize
that only by the labourers and Peasants Soviet can
they find their revolutionary emancipation. Any struggle
concerning the interests of individuals and not of a
political nature is called an economic struggle.
The line which separates an economic struggle from a
political one however, is not clearly defined. (Hai 23).

Plan of Struggle: It is not necessary to urge
the masses to work for a general political struggle
within a limited period but we should lead them to
labour at economic struggles. At this moment when
the revolutionary spirit is at its ebb we should put
forth slogans of 'determined victory' for our struggles
in order to arouse them from their cowardly and abject
spirit. In addition we should gain victories in the
small struggles in hand before we organize others and
not so extend them, in order to avoid failure.
Appeals and petitions should not be given too prominent a
position in the struggles—if they are successful,
the masses gain faith in the Kuomintang. Demonstrations
may be used whenever it is deemed necessary. (Hai 5).

- 51 -

Struggles should be organized in various localities,
in cities as well as in towns. The developments must
cover all sides equally and not centre in one particular
village or city. (Great 85).

Oppressions practiced in villages are comparatively
smaller in scope than those in cities. It is not
difficult to incite the peasants to attack cities wherein
live landlords and people of the ruling class, but it
is dangerous, and to do so will run the risk of failure
as the work in the city is still not strongly established
and that in the village not equally developed. We
should not therefore undertake such a trial at present.
(Great 85).

To organize and associate labourers' struggles
with those of peasants in the period of the 'Autumn
Harvest Struggle'. Labourers should lead the farm
villages in struggles and should not look upon the
'Autumn Harvest Struggle' as a mere peasant struggle
otherwise this struggle will lose its true meaning,
from the political point of view. (Hai 15).

In connection with the 'Autumn Harvest Struggle'
not only the peasants should be led in struggles but
the labourers in the city as well. They should, in order
to avoid being isolated and thereby causing failure,
associate with each other. (Hai 17).

Soldiers in villages are often in contact with
peasants, activities should also be carried out amongst
them in order to avoid any attack on the peasants
struggles in future.

The failure of many struggles in various localities
are accounted for by isolation in activity. Isolated
struggles are easily suppressed one by one by opponents,
Special notice therefore should be paid to this.
(Great 152).

Relation between Struggle and organization

In the course of the development of our group we
should carry out struggles. In the midst of these
struggles we should exert all our efforts to recommend
to our body the most active elements and the ringleaders
of the masses otherwise we will lose our revolutionary
spirit, never be able to establish our group within
the masses, nor will we be able to carry out any
activity amongst the masses or hope for the
materialization of our policy. (Great 81).

The organization in a long period of peace (that
is to say when no struggle has occurred) whereby
its comrades receive no training, is just like a building
on sand and will be easily destroyed when wind and rain
come. It is far from being bolshevized. (Great 45).

- 52 -

The victory in a struggle depends upon the strength
of unification of the masses. The by-gone struggles
which were conducted with unorganized people gave us
experience and proved that such struggles were useless.
We should strive for the organization work prior to
or during a struggle. (Great 85).

Special attention should be paid to the masses and
also that weapons are in order prior to the start of
a struggle although weapons are always standing by for
use. (Great 85).

Accurate statistics dealing with the number and
ability of members must be made. The organization of
the party will be developed during struggles, absorbing
and promoting brave and talented comrades. These
comrades will be assigned to reform and strengthen
administrative organs. (Duh Yi 3).

When the masses who have insufficient experience
in struggles, become disheartened with their own
efforts and grow tired of the daily struggles, we
should induce them to realize the meaning of 'class'
and their own strength by victory in small struggles
and help them to start off on the right track.
(Great 64).

Organize and extend such bodies as the anti-Japanese
League, Diplomatic Affairs Supervisory Committee, and
National Salvation Ten Men's Groups, utilizing them
as implements for open activities and concurrently for
carrying out struggles for the freedom of speech,
assembly and publication. (Great 132).

The Chief aim of our carrying out constant struggles
is to arouse sympathy amongst the masses. Besides
influencing the masses however, we should develope
the organization of the Group and the masses themselves.
Recently, in many struggles, instead of centralizing
your work in penetrating into the masses you devoted
all your attention to military activities. Whether
or not a struggle resulted in victory or failure
thereby, both the Party and the Group were unable
to carry on further struggles and the organization
of the Group even ran the risk of being eliminated.
This is not only a humiliation to our work but also
a loss. (Great 74).

The Group should absorb active elements with a view
to developing its organization, and foment struggles
in the course of its development. (Great 58).

When no struggle occurs the Group may continue
its development, but the peaceful state will cause the
organization to disintegrate and the comrades depressed
in spirit. We should therefore constantly fight against
any thought favouring peace with a view to preventing
the collapse of the organization. (Great 52).

- 53 -

Should the establishment and/or the strengthening
measures of the organization of the masses be overlooked
during a struggle, the masses will be but a disorganized
rabble. If the struggle becomes a failure dissension
among the masses will be the natural result; if victorious
the interests gained will be lost should the masses
be loosely organized masses. (Great 153).

Extend small struggles in connection with the
daily life of the labouring masses and absorb
labourers with a view to arousing the depressed
revolutionary spirit of the masses. (Hai 50).

In the evolution from economic struggles to

soldiers, people engaged in the salt business, and
shop assistants, the chief work is to extend our
organization. (Great 44).

Comrades who are members of students' unions

and select enthusiastic elements to join the Group.
It is not necessary to adopt the policy of 'comrades
struggle' but it is of importance to observe clearly
the evolution of circumstances, seizing opportunities
as they emerge therefrom to start struggles, which
we can turn into a partial or whole victory. (Great 60).

The Juvenile and young workers, apprentices and
shops assistants in Chekiang Province are all in an

The 'Brother Groups' should besides assisting
each other in military work, mutually help in economic

You, the several intellectual elements of the City

You should put forth demands dealing with the

-54-

Special Attention should be paid to the degree of

Relation between Struggle and Movement

In every struggle attention should be paid to the
slogans used. Should we lead labour and peasant masses

the labourers and peasants will become economists.
On the contrary should we lead them in political struggles
(Anti-Imperialist and anti-Kuomintang) without any
economic demands they will not persevere in the
struggles. So the most important thing in the struggles
is to let them know the revolutionary route of the
labour and peasant Soviet. (Duh Yi 4).

Propaganda Work: The labourers, peasants, and
soldiers should be informed of the news of uprisings
in various places with a view to setting them on the
way of struggle. (Tung 3).

Keep in contact with and penetrate into the masses.
Try to understand the daily life of the people and put
forth slogans containing demands in their interests
(such as refusal to pay rents and taxes, demands for
freedom of speech, assembly and publication) in order
to start daily struggles.

-55-

The Propaganda work should besides penetrating
the masses at the same time be extended
especially in a struggle. (Hai 15).

You should not put aside the mass struggle after

Guide various classes especially the labourers

Extend the non-payment of rentals, anti-Kuomintang

-56-

At present it is not known whether the rent
for the Autumn quarter at Wong-gnai (黃泥) has all been
paid or not. Should the answer be negative you should

fact that the Kuomintang deceives people with its
2 5 (?) reduction, and putting forth slogans advocating

end struggle. (Great 42).

work the chief thing is to progress from your propaganda

non payment of debts as well as taxes. (Great 43).

1. Try to obtain a comprehensive knowledge of the
daily struggles and start daily struggles, search out
the requirements of the labour masses in their daily
life and lead them to demand and obtain their
requirements from the capitalists.

2. We should not hope for the extension of a
struggle but its victory, so there should be no demands
in slogans which are impossible for us to attain.

3. Connection between struggle slogans and political
slogans:
a) adequate slogans for activities to be undertaken
be put forth in the struggle.
b) appended to these slogans adequate political
slogans be put forth.

4. Should the Kuomintang come to arbitrate in the
struggle we should
a) propagate that the judgement will not benefit
the labour masses.
b) propagate that the judgement will deceive the
labour masses.
c) propagate that the judgement will benefit the
capitalists.

Uprising

Uprising is not child's play. It is not a
thing that can be accomplished when we want it. If
we want to stage an uprising, we hope it will be
successful, and if we wish it to be successful, we
must attain the following conditions : Firstly we
must have a large organization, which must be organized
at any time - farmers join the peasants committee and
labourers the union. The larger the organization
grows, the more influential we will become. Secondly
we must have vigorous branches of our Party or Group.
In order to enable the Party to direct the people to
obey our command, it is necessary to make our branches
powerful and capable of holding meetings. For every
one of our colleagues to be able to proceed with
work without depending upon his leaders is of utmost
importance. Thirdly, we must have the public tendency
to rise up, so prior to an uprising, it is necessary
to rouse the determination of the public in order to
make them realize the necessity of uprisings and
nothing else. Fourthly, we must have struggles by
the public. Thus before the Canton Uprising, the
seamen's union declared a strike and farmers refused
to pay autumn rents. To start an uprising is just
the same as firing a cracker, the fuse must be lit
first and then the cracker will explode. Fifthly,
we must arm the public. Therefore labour corps,
peasants revolutionary armies and youth vanguards must
be formed. To fight and shoot must be practiced in
normal times. During an uprising everyone by means
of his own gun disarms his opponent. In this way,
weapons may be obtained. Sixthly, the uprising must
be started when the reactionaries are in a state of
abstraction. For example: if we start an uprising
when the Kuomintang members are fighting among them-
selves or there is a shortage of rice or food in
the market, the Kuomintang will be in a great fright
and will not know how to offer resistance. Now what
form shall be adopted for an uprising? If we have
attained all the above mentioned, how shall we start
our uprising? We can mention the following two ways:
(1) The direct partial occupation of land and (2) The
extension of guerrilla warfare resulting in partial
occupation. (Great 132)

Guerilla Warfare

What is guerilla warfare ? It is like this:
At a place where our power is not strong enough and
the peasant army is not well armed and yet the
struggle of the public has reached its zenith and
at the same time the reactionary party is still
able to defeat us with an army, we cannot therefore
occupy this area and are obliged to mobilize our
followers in various villages who will be advised
not to fight face to face with the reactionary
soldiers but to evade them and start riots and
uprising in other villages. They should be advised
to shift their activities from the original place
to other places on the arrival of the reactionary
soldiers. On the other hand sudden attacks are
to be made on these soldiers en route, disarm some
of them, seize their rice and extend our influence
from one place to another with a view to establishing
Soviet. But in guerilla warfare we should pay
attention to the following :

1. The Peasant army should be closely related to the
public.

2. On arrival at a village, the peasant army should
at once absorb the peasants of that village into
the army and start the uprising by killing the
land owners, corrupt gentry and loafers. But
they should not behave as bandits and loot in the
village. (Great 138).

The armed strength of the guerilla warfare
is secured through the regular attention of the
public. It is not to be an organization formed
by us by employing some persons as soldiers and
training them. The use of the guerilla warfare
is (1) To resist the armed force of the reactionary
party or to attack them as well as to support the
progress of the struggle of the people; (2) to
assist certain villages, where the work has not yet
been started but the neighbouring cities have been
so developed for the struggle that these places may
be occupied at any time, in starting the struggle;
(3) to start the uprising or assist the people to
rise up when the time is ripe but when the uprising
has not yet been started owing to certain oppression
or suppression. The guerilla warfare should always
be with the public unless during a critical period
when it is necessary to take shelter somewhere in
order to preserve the strength. (Great 85).

Guerilla warfare is one of the forms of the
struggle or new tactics in warfare. Although it
is closely related to struggle and the mass,
its main object is to extend the movement of the
masses and establish a more extensive revolutionary
area.

When a delay in starting the peasants' uprising
even for the purpose of making fuller preparations is
not permitted or little greater success can be achieved
from a material point of view, the Party should therefore
adopt the guerilla warfare (That is, cities or large

- 78 -

town are not to be occupied, nor any army be organized.
With a small number of men, incessant attacks are to
be made on the troops of the Government or the armed
force of the landlords) (Great 196).

At a place where the conflict between the
peasants and the upper classes is in a very
serious state, a small dispute in the daily
life should be developed into an armed encounter.
Consequently the guerilla warfare has become one
of the most important methods of struggle at these
places. Communists should therefore be more
determined to lead these struggles so as to make
them better organized. (Hai 51).

The resolutions passed at the 9th Meeting
of the Executive Committee of the Communist
Internationale points out that the peasants'
automatic guerilla warfare of one or a few hsien
in various provinces or districts can
become the starting point of the victory of the
people's uprising of the whole country under the
following condition. It is not absolutely
necessary to transform the guerilla warfare into
a local uprising. It can only be transformed when
a large number of peasant masses are mobilized
and when they are demanding the establishment of
their own political power of their own while the
reactionary influence is quickly waning.
Consequently when the guerilla warfare has been
extended to a larger area and due to the
participation of a big mass shown signs of
developing into a local uprising of a district
or Hsien, the Party should pay particular attention
to the strength, preparations, organizations,
plans and strategy in order to lead the labourers
and masses of the places and cooperate with them to
further the uprising. Efforts should be concentrated
to fulfil all slogans of struggle, exterminate all
reactionary influence with a view to materializing
the policy of the Soviet Political Power and above
all extending the limits of the uprising to the
adjoining cities or areas. (Hai 43 Great 159).

The main duties of guerilla warfare are to
(1) materialise the slogans of the peasants'
struggle (confiscate the land of the land
owners and divide it among the peasants;
massacre the landlords and corrupt gentry,
organize peasants' representative meetings
and Peasants' Soviet Political Power) and
extend the peasants' activities to the
revolutionary battle line.

(2) absorb the surviving courageous youths and
proletarians as well as semi-proletarians
into the guerilla warfare of the Red Army
with a view to enlarging it into a Labourers'
and Peasants' Revolutionary Red Army.

(3) Weaken the influence of the reactionaries by
disarming the volunteers and policemen etc.

- 71 -

The guerilla warfare therefore should be started
from the demands of the masses and conducted under the
leadership and organization of the masses. It should
be carried out in conjunction with propaganda and
inciting work. (Great 159).

With relations to the question of guerilla
warfare, the Central Notification in one part
points out "The guerilla warfare is started from
the mass struggle and must be used to aid the mass
struggle". At various places, however, the guerilla
warfare is still regarded as the Red Terror Method
of Incendiarism and Homicide which is independent
of the masses. Isolation from the masses will surely
give the reactionary influence a chance to launch an
attack, thereby discourging the masses in the struggle.
This mistake must be corrected. (Great 132).

Guerilla warfare is to be used to resist the
armed force of reactionaries in a mass struggle
(volunteers troops or policemen) or to attack the
reactionaries (disarming the landlords or gentry).
It is to use a small number of armed men to support
the mass struggle in order to make further progress.
Consequently it should not be separated from the
mass struggle and particular attention must be made
to create armed organization among the masses.
(Great 132).

Guerilla warfare also embodies the meaning of
starting the mass struggle. Therefore, under the
following circumstances we can and should send
guerilla groups to assist the peasants in the struggle:
(1) When in an occupied area (which requires external
extension) there are Red Army or Red Vanguards which
exist publicly, we should send Red Army Vanguards
to the neighbouring villages to incite the public
to struggle.

(2) At places where we have our labourers, peasants
and student armies, (such as Kian where there are
rifles), small groups should be sent to villages
to incite the public to start the struggle.

(3) At places where the peasants have already risen
up or have very high feelings for struggle but
occupation has not yet been carried out owing
to the suppression by certain reactionary
influence (volunteers and garrison) we can send
guerilla groups to assist in starting the uprising
and reinforcing the armed force of the guerilla
warfare.

The Party should also pay attention to the
armed strength of the peasants. Formerly we had
the peasants armed, we assembled them together
and formed a labourers and peasants revolutionary
army similar to the ordinary troops (once recruited
their families required money). As soon as we were
short of money, these armies were transformed into
bandit-like troops. This requires improvement.
(Great 132. 158).

- 72 -

The past guerilla warfare in various places
brought about many defects which were detrimental
to the development of the struggle or which even
destroyed it. Therefore we should try to amend these
wrongs in the following ways. Firstly, to prevent the
masses from being affected by the propaganda of
landowners and gentry leading them to look upon the
guerilla warfare as the acts of bandits. Consequently
guerilla warfare must be started at the request of the
masses and be under their leadership and organization.
It should be carried out in conjunction with propaganda
and inciting work. Secondly, the tendency to destroy
cities, and the aimless incendiarism and massacre, which
undoubtedly endanger the developments of the influence
of the Party among labourers and the masses, should be
eliminated. The Party should therefore endeavour to
do away with the tendency but should lead the struggles
of peasants in killing landowners and gentries and
weakening the influence of the reactionaries. The
aimless incendiarism and slaughter which has no
relation to the main work and no real benefits for
the revolution should be strongly opposed. Thirdly,
the present guerilla warfare is badly organized.
Therefore, well planned, organized and centralized
directions should be given (Peasants Cooperative
Association) (Hai 51).

When the masses' struggle-feelings are very
excited, several tens of persons may disarm the Peace
Reservation Corps and burn their houses as well
as massacre rowdies and evil gentry and confiscate
their properties, which should be distributed among
poor peasants. A meeting of a large number of
peasants and masses should then be immediately
convened to promulgate the general regulations of
land revolution and establish the Soviet. The land
deeds should be burnt publicly and the wrongs of
these rowdies denounced. Propaganda in favour of
the extension of Soviet land revolution should better
be carried out by the peasants committee if the
committee is well organized and has the trust of
farming masses.

Peasants struggles should not be carried out
by peaceful measures. We should make preparations
for an armed struggle of which guerilla warfare
is of the utmost importance. Guerilla warfare must
originate from the masses and should on no account
be seperated from the public, thus making it as an
independent military movement.

In the course of guerilla warfare and struggles,
the 'Group' should organize propaganda parties (of 3 or
5 persons each and not more than 6 persons) which should
carry out propaganda work as usual at places where the
mass movement has occurred in order that the inhabitants
there will not regard us as common troops or bandits.

There are not many provincial defence troops
at your place, and therefore you may start small armed
disturbances in villages where the force of the
defence army is small (N.B. the object of these
disturbances is to save us from being besieged) in
order to isolate the power of the troops and so that
even if we be surrounded, we may break through the
siege by our force. One of the following two ways
ways may be adopted according to circumstances.

- 73 -

(1) To scatter and go among the peasants in various
villages.

(2) To proceed to neighbouring villages or hsiens
where the military force is weak in order to
preserve our strength. If the troops (which
surround us) are incapable of destroying
us, we may remain inside, but accelerate the
progress of our work and establish relations
with work in neighbouring places.

The resolution points out that guerilla warfare
as well as uprising should be immediately started
in Chekiang South. Regarding this the Party should
therefore intensify the work in this district and
strengthen the relations among the Provincial
Committee and the ranks of the Party. (Great 191).

- 74 -

Partial Occupation

What is meant by direct partial occupation of land? It is this: In a province or at a certain place where our power is strong enough and the peasants army is well armed and the reactionary party is powerless to attack us, we then occupy this place and establish our government. If the reactionary party despatches troops to the place, we fight with them. For example: Hai Loh Poong, Kwang, was occupied in this way. (Great 138)

Partial occupation and occupation of cities or towns is not child's play. To occupy a city or a town you must pay attention to the following :
(for conditions of occupying a village see notice for Chicu Teu (autumn struggle ?) :-
a) Farming village struggles in this hsien have been developed and there is a possibility of establishing certain foundations of the masses in several villages or certain villages have been occupied and defended with appropriate armed force.
(b) Inside the city of the hsien, the city work has some foundations; labourers have good organization and armed forces; suitable work has been carried out in the reactionary troops and the bourgeoisie classes have been influenced by us.
(c) When the ruling class is very weak in power or is in a state of disintegration and incapable of maintaining its present state.
(d) There must be at least in the neighbouring hsians or several of them the possibility of occupying the area where the masses have established good foundation. In addition a careful military plan must be prepared. In short the mass movement is to be responsible for the occupation of a city while the military force is only to assist. You must not attempt the movement until you feel sure of your success nor when the mass is not in a position to receive our direction in full. We have some carefully considered matters and think that at present no cities should be occupied in Chekiang pending further developments in the work. Detailed conditions should be reported to the Provincial Committee and no movement should be started before permission is obtained from the Committee.

In an occupied area standing red armies and volunteer armies (?) are required. Red garrisons should be formed over a wide area.

Relation between Uprising and Struggle

The mass struggle needs not necessarily be in the form of military movement, although the final object of the Party and Group is to seize the political power and materialize the society of the Communist Party. It does not mean, however, that the political power must be seized as soon as the struggle has been started. The responsible comrades at various places have neglected to carefully study the significance of 'struggle' and consequently when a struggle is started, they have not secured sufficient numbers of the masses to do the work with the result that "all struggles are uprisings and none of the uprisings are successful". (Great 85).

- 75 -

Struggle need not necessarily be uprising. An
uprising is the continuation of a struggle and is the
development of the struggle to such a strong degree
that the political power is seized and the Soviet
established. Without daily training in struggle,
you cannot expect to start an uprising nor can you
start a sudden uprising without having maintained
and developed the daily struggle. As a matter of
fact the dicta "all struggles are uprisings", "one
uprising will be successful", "To be afraid to conduct
struggles" and "To be unwilling to conduct struggles"
are all the evil results of the blind-obedience-doctrine
and opportunism. (Great 65)

Having no clear idea of the difference between
struggle and uprising (no matter whether it is small
or large) you always consider struggle as uprising
with the result that you are afraid to conduct struggle
and the struggle therefore disappears altogether.
(Great 65).

The necessary conditions for a city uprising are :
(1) The excited revolutionary feelings of the labourers
and the development of their daily economic struggle.
(2) The disintegrating state of the ruling class.
(3) The hatred and bitterness against the citizens
(bourgeoisie) and where the downfall of the ruling class
has the public approvation.
(4) The preparation of the revolutionary strength of
the labouring class.

In fact the Party should never neglect the direction
of the economic and political struggle of labourers in
various hsiers, but redouble their efforts in this
movement. Taking advantage of every trifling dispute,
you should lead the labourers to start the struggle and
convince them of the importance of seizing the political
power by uprising and with the cooperation of the
peasants overthrowing the ruling class. These are
material preparations for a city uprising. The close
establishment of a relation between the labour uprising and
the peasant uprising rests heavily on the shoulders of the
Party. These single uprisings can never achieve any
success. (Great 196)

It is a great mistake to overlook the strength
of the labourers and peasants. The duty of the Party
is to lead and direct the daily struggle of the labourers
and teach them armed uprising. The city labour
uprising is the victory for the revolution. (Great 196)

Due to neglect of duty by the Hsien and town
Committees, the Peasants uprising and struggle became
independent. You must try to connect them although
they should carry on their work independently, so as
to facilitate the work of extension and making it more
difficult for our opponents to attack us.

It is pure blind-obedience to establish an
independent 'uprising committee' with branches at
various villages, because it means that without starting
the mass struggle you are thinking of obtaining victory
by means of military preparations. What a serious
mistake this is. You should at once correct it, other-
wise the 'Yung Kong Group' will result in tragic failure.
(Great 64)

- 76 -

Instead of considering the extension of the
activities to a larger area and developing the
struggle to uprising with a view to establishing
the Soviet foundation and executing the policy of
the Soviet, you instantly attack a city as soon as the
struggle is commenced and massacre the people, set
fire to property, and rob and loot. In short you
confine your activities to one place with the
result that the people are led to think that the
land revolution is no better than bandit activities
and does not work for the benefit of the peasants.
Consequently you can not maintain what success you have
attained. Your line may be easily broken through
by the enemy. (Great 153).

The uprising is to be developed from the daily
small struggle. Therefore comrades at various places
should seize every trifling matter and whenever there is
a chance for struggle start is without delay. In
addition to the rent and rice question which will easily
form an important struggle, you should seize every in-
cident of oppression or insulting of peasants by the
rowdies, policemen, troops such as disputes over one
cooper, etc, to start the struggle. No matter whether
there are only a few persons present at the beginning,
even one or two, just start the struggle, once, twice,
etc. and eventually the number of men will be greatly
increased, when the struggle can take form of
uprising. So at the beginning you need not commit
homicide or incendiarism; you just hold a
demonstration, quarrel with the oppressors and when
the number of man increases, then massacre rowdies,
disarm the troops, organize and enlarge the revolutionary
army, red garrison and youth vanguards. Propaganda on
land revolution and Soviet political power should then
be conducted thus inciting the revolutionary and
political feeling to a climax. In the end a village
or a town can be occupied and a Soviet political power
can be established.

You have neglected to start the daily struggle;
you have concentrated your attention on the preparations
for the big struggle or uprising. But you should
know that the daily struggle will stir up the
revolutionary spirit and enlighten the political
knowledge as well as strengthen the foundation of the
organization. Without these preliminaries, the
large struggle or uprising will not succeed in inciting
the public feeling. (Great 153)

If the peasant struggle struggle and the city
struggle are not related and do not cooperate together,
the peasant struggle can not develop independently
with the result that the success is almost certain to
disappear, (Great 153)

We should energetically lead the labour class and
their friends - poor people and the citizens - to beat
down the capitalists. During the struggle we should
put forwards various demands for the youth labourers.
It should be remembered that our directing power can
only be secured during the struggle and our closest
object is land revolution and city uprising, the
foundation of which must be laid in the struggle.
(Tung 3)

In future you should seize all opportunities to
use the slogan of "resist landtax, rent, demand increase

- 77 -

in wages" etc. to incite the feeling of the public
with a view to starting the daily struggle which will
be developed into an uprising. Before the outbreak,
extensive propaganda should be conducted among the
public so as to make it the desire of the public to
light the fuse. You should never start the movement
when the public are still ignorant of the meaning and
object. (Great 45)

Our comrades have abandoned the city work and
devoted their time to accelerating the commencement of the
uprising, while the peasants owing to oppression over
a long period will not believe in the fact that the
daily struggle will bring forth success with the result
that they are willing to undertake the work of uprising
once and for all. Consequently our comrades have no
time to correct this wrong idea. (Particularly the
Special Committee of West Chekiang) [Great 35).

The public is not a united body therefore every member
keeps his suffering to himself and having no experience
of struggle does not realize his own strength.
Consequently it is our duty to make him understand that
the only way to redress his sufferings is to unite with
others and stand on the same line to fight against
the ruling class and the capitalists. On the other
hand the Party and Group should have extensive
organization and strong determination to lead the public
through the struggle so as to make them understand that
our organization is fighting for the benefit of the
labourers and peasants. Our foundation will thereby
be consolidated and the public will therefore
willingly follow our leadership. (Great 85)

Peasants struggle and uprising will be unsuccessful
if no assistance is obtained from the labourers in
cities and villages. You should therefore commence
immediately the work among youth manual workers and
organize their unions. (Great 153)

At present there is no foundation of city work
in the whole province of Chekiang but only preparations
of military force in villages and therefore we have
no hope of city uprisings. You should not use
guerilla groups and heroic red terror such as assassi-
nation corps to rouse the public to attack cities as
these are too independent. (Great 85)

The duty of absorbing the masses is necessary
for armed uprising -- because to fulfil this duty
is the preliminary step of the new revolution. It
also means that the propaganda slogans of struggles
are changed into slogans of practical movement.

The Group should besides appointing a portion of
its brave labour comrades to participate in the military
training and secret organizations conducted by the
Party, make strong efforts to select radical elements
among youth labourers. (Sang 6)

Struggles should not be developed into uprising.
The highest object is to materialise the partial
occupation of villages. (Hai 5)

- 78 -

During the course of struggle, you should extend
as much as possible the work of red terror and pro-
paganda such as distributing handbills, killing land-
owners, rowdies and gentries, burning their houses and
confiscating their properties and then mass meetings
should be convened. You should form farm labourers
revolutionary corps and red garrisons and select some
strong peasants to participate in the movement so as to
conduct guerilla warfare and armed uprising. (Gr. 185)

Because it is difficult to conduct guerrila warfare
inside cities, you should not do so until uprising and
street skirmishes in the cities have commenced. (Great 196)

Struggle is important for guerrila warfare, and
military preparations in various villages and seizure of
enemy's weapons are important for struggle, so that
guerrila warfare cannot be declared without the public
support thus making it as indepent military movement.
Because guerrila warfare is different from armed
uprising or attacking of cities, you should not despise
the latter nor ignore mass work, and at the same time
you should not devote all your attention to the former.
(Great 93)

During the struggle (on the night of June 19) in
killing rowdies and gentries you have neglected the
following points. You did not make sufficient pre-
parations and carry out propaganda beforehand. Owing
to the fact that none of the masses participated in the
struggle but only several tens of our comrades, on the
following day the gentries and rowdies had all fled.
During that struggle though the reactionary force in
the city was feeble yet you did not extend the movement
by propaganda and excitement but nullified the struggle.
(Great 73)

Our comrades are all pleased to hear about and
conduct uprising, partial occupation and guerrila war-
fare. For this reason you disregard your daily work
and pay attention only to preparation of military
movement. Military preparation is, however, obtained
from daily work and is only a portion of the whole
preparation for uprising. Proletarians revolutions
and military movement depends entirely upon the masses.
Military opportunism is blind-obedience-doctrine, which
mistakes the Bolshevik Group should not commit You
have misunderstood the significance and action of the
struggle and forgotten to do your work which is the
basis of our Group. (Great 85).

Instead of attacking and occupying cities as soon
as you have led the masses to conduct the movement of
resisting rent payments, you should accelerate the
progress of our work in order to threaten and prevent
the landlords and ruling class from proceeding to the
villages to collect rent. In fact we will have occupied
these villages. Then you extend the organization of the
masses and develop the revolutionary influence and when
sufficient foundation is established you may start guerrila
warfare and occupy publicly --- remember that you should
not establish the Soviet before good mass foundation

- 79
is obtained, that is to say after the outbreak of
the movement to resist rent payment, we will
partially occupy the villages. We carry on our work
among the masses and when we have established found-
ations among the masses, we may further our
developments. (Great 74)
